title: The one-web-server rule governs the USER INTERFACE, not service ports — a device may listen to be called, it may not grow a second UI.
question: Ticket 548dd13fb4db (the one inference door speaks a second wire format) needs something LISTENING for a third-party agent's base_url to point at. CC's cast check (3) routed that to web_server's owner, reading the standing rule 'one web server, surfaces in the shim; a device gets a declared PANE, never its own server' as a bar on any device opening any port. That reading would have made the OpenAI-shaped door either impossible or a web_server dependency.
ruling: Akien, 2026-09-11, verbatim: 'the web server rule was because during theigors, you were creating seperate web servers on port after port for each device. akien hereby allows the exception because this is not the User Interface web server, this is a service port.'
what_the_rule_was_always_about: THE WHY, RECOVERED FROM ITS ORIGIN. The rule was born of a measured failure in TheIgors: CC stood up a separate web server per device, port after port, each with its own UI. The harm was a fragmented USER INTERFACE — one system presenting many faces at many addresses, with no single place for a person to stand. The rule's target is the FACE, not the socket. CC had preserved the rule's words and lost its why, which is the standing failure mode 'words kept, meanings replaced'.
the_distinction_that_now_governs: A UI SURFACE faces a person and must arrive through the one web server as a declared pane. A SERVICE PORT faces a machine — another process calling this one over a wire protocol — and is the ordinary shape of a device that can be called at all. A device may open a service port. A device may NOT stand up a second user interface. The test is who is on the other end: a person's browser, or a caller's client.
what_this_does_not_permit: It is an exception for SERVICE PORTS, not a repeal. A device that opens a port and then serves HTML pages to a human at it has done the exact thing TheIgors did, and this ruling does not cover it. Nor does it license a port per device by reflex: the inference door's port exists because a third-party harness can only be configured with a base_url, which is a measured constraint of the consumer, not a convenience for the builder.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel — the rule's why was already settled in TheIgors and CC re-derived it wrongly rather than reading it)
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — this distinction is prose today and is an IOU until something can tell a UI surface from a service port)
CP4 (the laws serve us; when they chafe it is time to review — the rule chafed against a legitimate build and the review recovered its scope rather than weakening it)
affects: 548dd13fb4db — the one inference door speaks a second wire format: cast check (3) is CLOSED by this ruling. The door may open its own service port; it does not route to web_server's owner.
cb97524c0e8e — hermes runs as a device beside CC: hermes' own gateway process listens, and by this ruling that is a service port, not a second UI.
The standing rule as CC held it in memory ('one web server, surfaces in the shim') is not repealed but SCOPED: it governs panes and faces, not sockets.
owed_physics: NONE BUILT, and the IOU is named rather than implied. Nothing today can distinguish a service port from a UI port — the distinction is who is on the other end, which no sieve currently reads. Until something can, this is prose and therefore a tracked debt, not a resting state (Law 4). The cheapest checkable shape, unbuilt and unratified: a device that binds a port declares it in its charter with its wire protocol, and a sieve reds a device serving text/html at a port declared as a service one.
provenance: Raised by CC at the /sorted cast of 548dd13fb4db on 2026-09-11, as cast check (3) — the one question a builder could not settle alone. Akien ruled it in the same conversation, correcting CC's reading of the rule by naming its origin in TheIgors.
the_ruling_verbatim: the web server rule was because during theigors, you were creating seperate web servers on port after port for each device. akien hereby allows the exception because this is not the User Interface web server, this is a service port.
now_the_spec_says: The one-web-server rule governs the USER INTERFACE. A device may open a SERVICE PORT to be called by another process; it may not stand up a second human-facing UI. The test is who is on the other end: a person, or a caller.
